tooltip.radiocraft.antenna_analyzer: Used for analyzing antenna networks and handheld radio antennas
tooltip.radiocraft.antenna_connector: Joins antenna wires and coax: a wire holder you can also run coax into.
tooltip.radiocraft.antenna_pole: Holds the end of an antenna wire. Use antenna wire on this and another holder to string a wire between them.
tooltip.radiocraft.antenna_splitter: Receive only: coax from one antenna to several radios on its other sides. Each hears the antenna, a little weaker; none can transmit through it.
tooltip.radiocraft.antenna_switch: One radio, three antennas: the brass input turns to the radio's coax by itself. Right click to switch between outputs 1, 2 and 3.
tooltip.radiocraft.antenna_tuner: Put it anywhere on the coax between a radio and its antenna. Turn its three dials until the lamp is solid green: red blinks faster as you get closer, yellow-green below SWR 3. The further off resonance the antenna, the more power is lost in the tuner.
tooltip.radiocraft.auto_tuner: Put it on the coax between a radio and its antenna, with power. Tunes itself whenever the radio changes band or moves 1 MHz. Shows TUNE FAIL on the radio when the antenna is too far off.
tooltip.radiocraft.balun_four_to_one: Feed point for off-centre-fed dipoles (short arm a third to two thirds of the long one, matched on the even harmonics too) and delta loops.
tooltip.radiocraft.balun_nine_to_one: Feed point for a random wire: one wire of any shape, at least half a wavelength long. Needs an antenna tuner.
tooltip.radiocraft.balun_one_to_one: Feed point for dipoles, inverted Vs, end-feds, quarter wave verticals and Moxons.
tooltip.radiocraft.charge_controller: Sits between solar panels and batteries and manages the charge. Wire panels in and batteries out.
tooltip.radiocraft.coax_wire: Carries the signal between a radio and its antenna's balun. Runs along the ground, up walls and over steps.
tooltip.radiocraft.corded_microphone: On its radio's cord: hold right click to talk, right click the radio to hang it up. The cord reaches 5 blocks.
tooltip.radiocraft.crystal_poor: Poor crystal: a little more noise, and it drifts off frequency.
tooltip.radiocraft.crystal_pure: Pure crystal: a little less noise.
tooltip.radiocraft.data_wire: Links a radio to accessories, wired speakers and stations that are not beside it. Carries no power. Runs along the ground, up walls and over steps.
tooltip.radiocraft.direction_finder: Stack 3 to 8 direction finder modules against it, each with the same kind of antenna, and tune to a signal.
tooltip.radiocraft.direction_finder_modu: One antenna input of a direction finder: coax to an antenna, and stack it against the direction finder or another module.
tooltip.radiocraft.dummy_load: A perfect match on every band that hardly radiates: about 10 blocks. Fits on a radio or its coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.five_btv_antenna: Trap vertical, seven blocks tall: matched on every HF band and VHF. On HF it sends its power low, so it reaches less by line of sight and further by skip. Coax goes to the base.
tooltip.radiocraft.folded_dipole_antenna: Commercial two-bay 2m folded dipole for towers: 25% more gain than a J-pole, and DC grounded, so lightning seldom does damage.
tooltip.radiocraft.handheld_direction_fi: Right click to set the frequency. Held, it beeps faster the more you face a station transmitting there.
tooltip.radiocraft.hf_manpack: A QRP 10m/20m SSB and CW radio you carry. Wear it (sneak right click), open it with right click or the Open Worn Manpack key.
tooltip.radiocraft.hf_radio_10m: HF transceiver for the 10m band (28 MHz). SSB voice and CW. Needs a 10m antenna on coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.hf_radio_20m: HF transceiver for the 20m band (14 MHz). SSB voice and CW. Needs a 20m antenna on coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.hf_radio_40m: HF transceiver for the 40m band (7 MHz). SSB voice and CW. Needs a 40m antenna on coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.hf_radio_80m: HF transceiver for the 80m band (3.5 MHz). SSB voice and CW. Needs an 80m antenna on coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.hf_receiver: Listens on the HF bands. Receive only.
tooltip.radiocraft.ionosonde: Sounding antenna for the Ionospheric Processor. On a radio it hears VHF well but matches poorly everywhere, worst on HF.
tooltip.radiocraft.ionospheric_processor: Coax to an Ionosonde Antenna lets it read the sky. Through a radio it touches it answers solar weather requests and warns of blackouts.
tooltip.radiocraft.j_pole_antenna: VHF antenna for 2m base stations and repeaters. Connect it with coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.large_battery: Stores power for the station: charged from a charge controller, it runs the radios on its wire. Batteries wired together share charge evenly.
tooltip.radiocraft.loudspeaker: Run wire from a radio to it: plays the radio loud enough to hear far away, with some distortion.
tooltip.radiocraft.manpack_mic: Hold right click to talk. Sneak right click hangs it back up.
tooltip.radiocraft.map_direction_finder: A direction finder that plots its fix on a map of the world.
tooltip.radiocraft.microphone: Stands beside a radio. Hold right click on it to talk; sneak and right click to lock talking on. Speak close: it gets quieter as you step away. Lets go after a timeout.
tooltip.radiocraft.microwave_dish: One end of a microwave link: coax it to a microwave radio and point it at the other end's dish.
tooltip.radiocraft.microwave_radio: A digital point to multipoint link over microwave dishes on its coax. Carries APRS between H19s, bearings between direction finders, and telephone calls.
tooltip.radiocraft.old_tower_foothold: Weathered. Now and then one gives way under a climber.
tooltip.radiocraft.pabx: The exchange for telephones touching it or on its data wire, where there is no microwave radio: they can call each other. Needs power; gives its phones extensions from 100. A microwave radio is its own PABX.
tooltip.radiocraft.parrot_controller: Repeats received messages back out the connected radio. Affectionately called a "parrot" repeater.
tooltip.radiocraft.passthrough: Use on a plain solid block: it keeps its look but lets wire and coax run straight through it. Break it to get both back.
tooltip.radiocraft.premium_speaker: Place it touching a radio: the radio's whole audio range, as clean as it gets.
tooltip.radiocraft.qrp_radio_20m: Low power 20m transceiver: shorter range, lighter to build. Needs a 20m antenna on coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.qrp_radio_40m: Low power 40m transceiver: shorter range, lighter to build. Needs a 40m antenna on coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.radio_fax: Faxes books, paper, maps and enchanted books to another fax by callsign, through the radio it touches or its station's radio interface. Stock it with paper, books and maps for what it receives.
tooltip.radiocraft.ringo_antenna: Commercial 2m vertical: 10% more gain than a J-pole, and DC grounded, so lightning seldom does damage.
tooltip.radiocraft.slim_jim_antenna: VHF antenna for 2m base stations and repeaters. Connect it with coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.small_battery: A common small battery, typically starts with 50-70% charge
tooltip.radiocraft.solar_panel: Makes power in daylight. Wire it to a charge controller.
tooltip.radiocraft.speaker: Place it touching a radio: the radio sounds fuller than through its own little speaker.
tooltip.radiocraft.telephone: Put it on a microwave radio or a powered Phone PABX (touching, or on its data wire) and dial another phone's extension. Sneak and right click to pick up the handset; place it on the side of a block to hang it on the wall.
tooltip.radiocraft.telephone_handset: On its phone's cord: talk into it during a call. Sneak and right click the phone to hang up. The cord reaches 5 blocks.
tooltip.radiocraft.teletype: RTTY through the radios it touches, printed on its own paper. SOLAR WX prints the solar conditions, which it reads through a radio with an antenna (not a dummy load) next to it. A comparator reads 1 (blackout) to 6 (great).
tooltip.radiocraft.teletype_roll: Torn off a teletype. Right click to read it; right click a teletype with an empty roll to feed it back in.
tooltip.radiocraft.tower_beacon_controll: Flashes a tower's lights: a redstone signal two seconds on, two seconds off. Found on towers.
tooltip.radiocraft.tower_foothold: A rung for climbing a tower, or standing on. Place it against a wall like a ladder.
tooltip.radiocraft.vhf_base_station: 2m FM transceiver for local contacts and repeaters. Needs a VHF antenna on coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.vhf_handheld_battery_: Click battery on VHF Handheld to swap batteries
tooltip.radiocraft.wall_speaker: Run wire from a radio to it: plays the radio here. Several can share one radio. A little rough.
tooltip.radiocraft.waterproof_wire: Power wire that can be laid under water. Runs along the ground, up walls and over steps.
tooltip.radiocraft.weather_station: Put it up high in the open. Any H19 APRS terminal within 64 blocks sends its weather in its beacons.
tooltip.radiocraft.wefax_receiver: Put a radio with an antenna beside it and paper in it: prints weather charts and the solar report.
tooltip.radiocraft.wire: Carries power between solar panels, charge controllers, batteries and radios. Runs along the ground, up walls and over steps.
tooltip.radiocraft.wire_bundle: Use on a wire of another kind to lay both in one block (up to 7). Sneak + right click a bundle with an empty hand to take one out.
tooltip.radiocraft.wire_junction: Joins power wire of any colour run into it. Not coax.
tooltip.radiocraft.world_map_module: Craft it with a direction finder to plot fixes on a map. Cartographers sell them.
tooltip.radiocraft.yagi_antenna: Directional VHF antenna: strongest in the direction it points. Connect it with coax.
